newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai PM says no change in finance portfolios.
newsitem.headline: Thai PM says no change in finance portfolios.

text.p: Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh said on Sunday after a special four-hour meeting of the Council of Economic Advisers that the team running country's finances would remain in office.
"The meeting has reached the conclusion that there will be no change in the area of the officials who are responsible for the economic affairs," he told reporters.
Chavalit's comments came amid concerns over a sharp slowdown in economic growth, low exports and questions over how the government was handling a crisis of confidence in the finance sector.
Rumours had circulated last week, as the Thai stock market tumbled to new 6-1/3 year lows, that such leaders as unelected Finance Minister Amnuay Virvan might be replaced.
Amnuay was not present at Sunday's meeting as he was attending the Asian Development Bank meeting in Japan.

Chavalit, who is also defence minister but does not hold any economic portfolios, said he would consult his economic advisers more to implement government measures to try to speed up economic recovery.
He reiterated comments made on Friday by central bank officials that there would be no baht devaluation or any change in the exchange rate mechanism.
